thread:
zoe_support: FYI customer (NimbleRetail) reporting sudden spike in latency + intermittent 403s since yesterday evening. They say requests are hitting eu region even though their org is pinned to us-west-2.

zoe_support: They pasted a curl from their infra showing Host resolves to inference.eu.redwood.ai and X-Forwarded-For shows our eu NAT IP. Billing team flagged higher per-token rate. Customer pretty unhappy. SUP-4521 created.

sam_oncall: can you paste the raw curl + any proxy headers? also want traceroute from their edge.

zoe_support: paste from customer (redacted):
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \ 
  -H 'Host: api.redwood.example' \ 
  https://inference.redwood.example/v1/generate
* Connected to inference.redwood.example (52.16.23.11) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.example
> User-Agent: curl/7.64.1
> X-Forwarded-For: 18.142.31.90
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< x-region: eu-west-1
< x-proxy-nat: 34.85.123.201
```

matt_network: x-proxy-nat looks like one of our eu peered egress IPs. do they use private-dedicated with hub peering?

zoe_support: yes private deployment (VPC) with peered hub. customer says they recently changed on-prem SD-WAN config but insisted egress should stay in us-west.

matt_network: ok likely SNAT on hub side is rewriting src => picks EU egress when hashing sessions. can you get `traceroute -n` from their app node and `ip route get 8.8.8.8`? also any NAT table (`sudo iptables -t nat -L -n`) or proxy bind configs would help.

li_devops: another quick repro: from a customer bastion, run
```
curl -v -H 'Host: api.redwood.example' \ 
  --resolve 'inference.redwood.example:443:52.16.23.11' \ 
  https://inference.redwood.example/v1/health
```
this forces DNS->IP; check response headers for x-region/x-proxy-nat. if it shows eu IP then the session is being hairpinned into eu hub.

zoe_support: customer ran traceroute, pasted:
```
traceroute to inference.redwood.example (52.16.23.11), 30 hops max
 1 10.0.0.1  0.5 ms 0.6 ms 0.4 ms
 2 192.168.254.1  1.2 ms 1.1 ms 1.0 ms
 3 34.85.123.201  42.3 ms 41.8 ms 42.0 ms
 4 52.16.23.11  42.9 ms 43.1 ms 42.7 ms
```

matt_network: hop 3 is our eu NAT (34.85.123.201). That explains it. Why would their traffic be routed to that NAT? check vpc-route table on their side and any TGW/peering route priorities.

eva_account: Customer upset about billing for eu region tokens. can we credit difference while we investigate? they lost real-time shopping latency.

li_devops: for quick mitigation we can add a per-org egress policy to prefer us-west egress IPs for their org id. pushing small route policy to the private control plane should take effect fast. I'll prepare a canary change then rollback if it causes churn.

li_devops: rollout id ROLLOUT-7725. applying to 3 private hubs (us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1) with priority override. will monitor.

sam_oncall: while that's rolling, can customer update endpoint host header to force us-west? not ideal but as temporary: set Host -> us-west.inference.redwood.example and --resolve to us-west ip.

zoe_support: customer confirmed mitigation reduced p95 latency from ~420ms to ~58ms and no more 403s. billing team issued pro-rated credit for EU tokens.

matt_network: root cause: their SD-WAN vendor changed NAT translation range causing source IPs to land in a hash bucket mapped to eu hub. hub health-check saw fewer sessions on us-west and moved affinity. fix: adjust SNAT mapping + add explicit org egress preference in control plane + patch hub health-check to include session-weighted metric.

zoe_support: follow-ups: 1) engineering to patch hub health-check 2) account ops to finalize credit 3) outreach doc to customers about SD-WAN SNAT caveat 4) close SUP-4521 after postmortem.

sam_oncall: thanks all. marking as resolved for now — please add any postmortem notes. :thumbsup:
